ahmedabad_walled_city.name: Ahmedabad Walled City
ahmedabad_walled_city.unescoStatus: UNESCO World Heritage City (2017) — First in India
ahmedabad_walled_city.founded: 1411 CE by Sultan Ahmed Shah I of the Muzaffarid Sultanate
ahmedabad_walled_city.significance: Ahmedabad's historic walled city is an outstanding example of Hindu-Muslim-Jain architectural and cultural synthesis spanning over 600 years.
keyFacts: Founded in 1411 CE — over 600 years of continuous habitation
First Indian city inscribed as UNESCO World Heritage City (2017)
Famous for intricate wooden architecture in traditional 'pol' neighbourhoods
Houses significant Islamic, Hindu, and Jain monuments
Traditional craft traditions including patola weaving, block printing, and bead work still practised

architecture.polSystem: Pols are traditional residential clusters, a unique urban form of Ahmedabad. Each pol has a large entrance gate, bird feeding platforms, community wells, and shared gathering spaces. The houses feature intricately carved wooden facades with jharokhas (oriel windows) and unique ventilation systems.

keyBuildings.Jama Masjid: Built in 1423 by Ahmed Shah I. Features 260 columns and 15 domes. One of the finest examples of Gujarati-Islamic architecture.
keyBuildings.Sidi Saiyyed Mosque: Built in 1573. Famous for its intricately carved stone lattice (jaali) windows depicting the Tree of Life — among the finest stone carvings in India.
keyBuildings.Bhadra Fort: Built in 1411 by Ahmed Shah. The original fortified palace complex from which the city grew.
keyBuildings.Adalaj Stepwell: 5-storey stepwell built in 1499. Multi-religion carvings representing the synthesis of Hindu and Islamic art.
keyBuildings.Teen Darwaza: The triple gateway built in 1415. Connected to the royal square and Maidan Shah.

polHouses.description: Pols are unique to Ahmedabad and represent one of the world's earliest examples of planned urban housing with communal facilities.
characteristics: Intricate wooden carvings identifying family/community identity

visitingTips.heritageWalk: Official Heritage Walk departs at 7:30 AM daily from Swaminarayan Temple, Kalupur
visitingTips.duration: Full exploration: 2-3 days. Quick tour: 3-4 hours
visitingTips.foodTips: Ahmedabad is famous for its vegetarian cuisine. Must try: Gujarati thali, khandvi, dhokla, and Manek Chowk street food at night

conservationChallenges: Wooden facades deteriorating due to weather, insects, and lack of maintenance
Increasing vehicular traffic causing structural vibration
Population pressure leading to overcrowding of historic structures
Informal construction and modifications to heritage buildings
Inadequate storm drainage causing periodic flooding
Limited awareness among residents about conservation obligations

modhera_sun_temple.name: Modhera Sun Temple
modhera_sun_temple.status: Protected Monument under Archaeological Survey of India
modhera_sun_temple.built: 1026-1027 CE during the reign of King Bhimdev I of the Solanki (Chaulukya) dynasty
modhera_sun_temple.significance: One of the finest surviving examples of Solanki temple architecture. The temple's precise astronomical alignment and extraordinary sculptural programme make it a masterpiece of medieval Indian art and science.
keyFacts: Built in 1026 CE — nearly 1000 years old
Designed with precise astronomical alignment: the rising sun illuminates the sanctum on equinoxes
The Surya Kund has exactly 108 shrines — the sacred number in Hindu tradition
After Mahmud of Ghazni's invasion, the temple was never used for worship
Now hosts the Modhera Dance Festival (Uttarayan) — a national cultural event
Dedicated to Surya, the Sun God

threeParts.Kund: Surya Kund (also called Rama Kunda) — the magnificent stepwell with 108 miniature shrines arranged in tiers around its perimeter
threeParts.SabhaMandap: The assembly hall (sabha mandap) — an elaborately carved open pillared hall used for gatherings and performances
threeParts.GarbhaGriha: The sanctum (garbha griha) — the innermost shrine where the Sun God's idol was placed, aligned for sunrise illumination

materials: No use of mortar — dry stone construction
architecture.astronomicalAlignment: The temple's east-west axis is aligned so that during the summer and winter solstices, and spring and autumn equinoxes, the first rays of the rising sun illuminate the sanctum's central image

suryaKund.description: The Surya Kund (stepwell) is a masterpiece of geometric design with tiers of steps descending to a central tank. Around the perimeter are 108 small shrines.
suryaKund.significance: The number 108 is sacred in Hindu and Jain traditions. The kund served for ritual bathing and water storage.

sculptures.description: The temple features an extraordinary programme of stone carvings covering virtually every surface — one of the richest sculptural schemes in Indian art.
subjects: Apsaras — celestial dancers in 108 different poses
Dikpalas — guardians of the eight directions

visitingTips.soundLightShow: Evening sound and light show (check ASI website for current schedule)
visitingTips.howToReach: Modhera is 100 km from Ahmedabad. Regular buses from Mehsana and Ahmedabad.

conservationChallenges: Stone weathering from monsoon rains and extreme summer heat
Biological growth (algae, moss) on stone, especially near Surya Kund
Visitor footfall causing surface abrasion on steps and carved panels
Insufficient drainage around the stepwell leading to moisture accumulation
Vibration damage from nearby road construction

conservation_terms.consolidation: Application of chemical or physical treatments to stabilize deteriorating stone or structural elements
conservation_terms.grouting: Injection of material into cracks to seal and strengthen
conservation_terms.desalination: Process of removing soluble salts from masonry to prevent crystallization damage
conservation_terms.biocide: Chemical treatment to remove and prevent biological growth (algae, moss, lichen)
conservation_terms.NDVI: Normalized Difference Vegetation Index — satellite imagery analysis technique to measure vegetation coverage
conservation_terms.ASI: Archaeological Survey of India — the primary body responsible for protecting India's heritage monuments
conservation_terms.bufferZone: The protected area around a heritage site within which development is restricted
conservation_terms.pol: Traditional residential cluster unique to Ahmedabad, featuring a communal entrance gate and shared community spaces

general: Respect the heritage structures — do not touch carved surfaces
Photography is permitted for personal use; commercial photography requires permission
Do not litter — carry your waste back
Dress modestly when visiting religious sites
Hire an official guide for the most informative experience
ahmedabad: Heritage Walk departs at 7:30 AM from Swaminarayan Temple, Kalupur
Avoid visiting during peak noon hours in summer (temperature can reach 42°C)
Manek Chowk transforms into a night food market after 9 PM
modhera: Visit at sunrise for the best experience of the solar alignment
The Modhera Dance Festival (January) is the best time to visit
Climbing on temple structures is prohibited
Evening sound and light show available most evenings
